弔.meaning: When the old archer dies, her friends lash her <part>bow</part> to a tall <part>pole</part> at the village gate, its string loose and a black ribbon tied round it. All week people stop by, pat the pole and leave a kind note for her grandson. The pole fills up with <kanji>condolences</kanji>.
弔.on: Her grandson wears her old bead <sound>cho</sound>ker under his collar, in her memory.
弔.kun: The village carves her a <sound>to</sound>tem pole, a cow bows with a soft '<sound>Mu</sound>', and the cook serves bowls of <sound>ra</sound>men in her name.

倉.meaning: A hungry building at the docks has an <part>umbrella</part> roof and a wide <part>mouth</part> for a door. Each morning the boss raises a <part>flag</part>, paints <part>one</part> <part>slash</part> on the wall for every ship, and the mouth swallows crates of tea and rope until dark. Sailors call this warehouse a <kanji>godown</kanji>.
倉.on: Its floor is so clean that the night guard polishes it with a bar of <sound>so</sound>ap.
倉.kun: A <sound>coo</sound>k sneaks in after dark to borrow a crate of <sound>ra</sound>men noodles.

荘.meaning: A <part>robust</part> old sailor retires to the hills and builds a cabin with a roof of thick green <part>grass</part>. Goats graze on top while he lies in a hammock below with lemonade. Friends come for long holidays. It's a little cabin, but he calls it his <kanji>villa</kanji>.
荘.on: Guests wash in an outdoor tub with a bar of <sound>so</sound>ap as big as a brick.
荘.kun: He waters the roof with a garden <sound>ho</sound>se, then locks the gate with a big brass <sound>key</sound>.

汁.meaning: A stingy cook drops <part>ten</part> peas into a pot of <part>water drops</part> and stirs. Ten guests arrive with ten spoons. Each one fishes out exactly one pea, sips the hot water and smiles politely. It's mostly water, but he calls it <kanji>soup</kanji>.
汁.on: One guest finds a <sound>jew</sound>el at the bottom of her bowl instead of a pea.
汁.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p laps up the leftovers, and a <sound>roo</sound>k drinks straight from the ladle.

殴.meaning: A polite <part>maiden</part> in a frilly skirt curtseys to the bully who has been stealing lunches all over the <part>ward</part>, then swings her heavy handbag and knocks his hat into the fountain. Shocked shopkeepers call it <kanji>assault</kanji>; the rest of the block calls her a hero.
殴.on: The bully hides up an <sound>o</sound>ak tree until she has gone home.
殴.kun: Up there he nibbles a <sound>na</sound>an, while a <sound>goo</sound>se honks at him from below.

乞.meaning: A seal sits at the end of the <part>diving board</part> at the public pool, flapping and barking at every swimmer with a sandwich. When nobody shares, it slides down the <part>zigzag</part> water slide and tries again from the top. All afternoon it does nothing but <kanji>beg</kanji>.
乞.on: A <sound>ko</sound>ala lifeguard sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and drops it a crust.
乞.kun: Next it begs a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala on a towel for the rest of its lunch.

酵.meaning: Out of <part>filial piety</part>, a son helps his grandpa down to the cellar every week to check the jars of cabbage. One jar has swollen like a stick of <part>dynamite</part>, fizzing and bubbling. Grandpa beams: 'Ready!' The cabbage has turned sour by <kanji>fermentation</kanji>.
酵.on: The lid pops off, shoots up the stairs and lands on an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne.

尚.meaning: The village's only <part>TV set</part> sits in the square with a <part>sparkle</part> of tinsel on top. Everyone bows as they pass, dusts it and brings it flowers. It hasn't worked for years, but it is still held in great <kanji>esteem</kanji>.
尚.on: Once a year someone plugs it in, and the whole village watches the same old <sound>show</sound>.
尚.kun: Grandma offers it a <sound>na</sound>an and taps the screen. '<sound>Oh</sound>, still not on,' she sighs.

妖.meaning: A <part>woman</part> at the fair wears a <part>tilted hat</part> covered in silver moths. Whenever she tips it, every moth in town flutters toward her, and so do the bees and the stray cats. She doesn't say a word. She is just strangely <kanji>attractive</kanji>.
妖.on: She does tricks with a glowing <sound>yo</sound>-yo, and the moths spin round it.
妖.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' says a guard, eyeing the moths and the ball of <sound>ya</sound>rn under her hat: suspicious.

辱.meaning: A proud golfer swings her <part>golf club</part> on a seaside course in front of a big crowd. A <part>clam</part> on the sand snaps shut on the club's head, and she waves it about, red-faced, with the clam clinging on. The crowd giggles. Nothing could <kanji>embarrass</kanji> her more.
辱.on: A <sound>jo</sound>gger stops to laugh, and so does the <sound>cu</sound>ckoo in the clubhouse clock.
辱.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' hoots a caddie, juggling a yu<sound>zu</sound>, and a <sound>ca</sound>rp in the pond and a <sound>shee</sound>p on the green join in.

幾.meaning: A baker carries two trays of sugar <part>twist</part> buns past a <part>sentry</part> at the castle gate. 'Halt! The tax is one bun in ten. How many?' The baker shrugs. The sentry counts, loses track, eats one and starts again. By noon he's full and still asking: '<kanji>how many</kanji>?'
幾.on: At last he locks both trays in the guardhouse with a big brass <sound>key</sound>.
幾.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' squeals the castle <sound>coo</sound>k when she finds the trays empty.

憂.meaning: A retired clown sits on a <part>folding chair</part> at the end of the pier, a <part>blanket</part> over his knees and a paper <part>heart</part> in his lap. He counts a <part>hundred</part> waves, sighs, and counts a hundred more. The seagulls leave him alone with his <kanji>melancholy</kanji>.
憂.on: A <sound>u</sound>nicorn trots down the pier and sits beside him without a word.
憂.kun: He stirs a cold bowl of <sound>u</sound>don and stares at the <sound>re</sound>d sunset.

賓.meaning: A palace throws a ball under its golden <part>roof</part>. The doors open, and in rides a <part>little</part> hermit crab on a tray made from a giant <part>shellfish</part>, a red sash in one bold <part>slash</part> across its shell. The king himself bows. Everyone wants to shake a claw with the <kanji>V.I.P.</kanji>
賓.on: The palace doors swing open on one huge golden <sound>hin</sound>ge just for it.
賓.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>, look!' whispers a child, as the crab is handed a red <sound>ro</sound>se and rides home on a <sound>do</sound>lphin.

叙.meaning: A king has <part>too much</part> gold in his vaults, so he melts some into shiny medals shaped like a <part>pretzel</part>. He hangs one round the neck of every baker, poet and dog in town. It takes all week. Never has a king had so many honours to <kanji>confer</kanji>.
叙.on: The last medal goes to a <sound>jo</sound>gger who runs in late, still puffing.
叙.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' sneezes the king, and the dog squeaks '<sound>Ee</sound>!' as the medal tickles its nose.

湖.meaning: Every night a tired, <part>old</part> <part>moon</part> sinks down from the sky to soak its aching craters. Its <part>water drops</part> splash over the hills and gather in a valley, cool and still. By morning the moon is gone, but its bath stays behind as a <kanji>lake</kanji>.
湖.on: A sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala paddles out on a log to look for moon dust.
湖.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat floats a yu<sound>zu</sound> and a bowl of <sound>u</sound>don across it to another <sound>mee</sound>rkat on the far shore.

擁.meaning: A sailor drops his <part>anchor</part> in the harbour, and a soaked <part>sparrow</part> flutters onto the cooking pot's <part>lid</part>, shivering. He tucks it into his beard, adds a <part>scribble</part> to the logbook, 'one new crew', and squeezes it gently. Every bird deserves a <kanji>hug</kanji>.
擁.on: To cheer it up he spins a <sound>yo</sound>-yo, and the sparrow rides the string round and round.

丘.meaning: A woodcutter swears to stop chopping trees, so he buries his <part>axe</part> under <part>one</part> long heap of earth. Grass grows over it, sheep lie on it, kids roll down it. Only the handle pokes out of the top like a flagpole. His promise became a gentle <kanji>hill</kanji>.
丘.on: Kids slide down it on a tea tray, steering with a pool <sound>cue</sound>.
丘.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps a sheep, as a kite shaped like a <sound>ca</sound>rp snags on the axe handle.

咲.meaning: An <part>alien</part> lands in a grey car park and opens its wide <part>mouth</part> to say hello. Instead of words, out pour petals: pink, white and gold. They take root in the cracks, and by the time it flies off the whole car park has begun to <kanji>blossom</kanji>.
咲.on: People drive for miles to see the car park's flower <sound>show</sound>.
咲.kun: A cat stretches out among the flowers, nibbling a <sound>sa</sound>rdine.

鎮.meaning: A dragon storms through the market, roaring. A tiny hypnotist steps up, swings a <part>gold</part> coin on a string and whispers, 'It's <part>true</part>, you're very sleepy.' The dragon's eyes droop and it curls up by the fish stall. One coin was enough to <kanji>tranquilize</kanji> it.
鎮.on: It snores with its huge <sound>chin</sound> resting on the coin.
鎮.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p tucks a blanket over it, and the hypnotist sets a yu<sound>zu</sound> by its nose to smell.

魂.meaning: Every night a <part>ghost</part> sits on the church roof flying a <part>kite</part>. Tied to its tail is something faint and glowing that hums. It isn't the ghost's body; that's long gone. It's the part of him that still loves kites: his <kanji>soul</kanji>.
魂.on: A <sound>con</sound>dor circles the kite, curious about the hum.
魂.kun: He shares a <sound>ta</sound>co with a lla<sound>ma</sound>, a <sound>shee</sound>p and an <sound>ee</sound>l, who all haunt the roof with him.

嬢.meaning: A <part>woman</part> who runs a laundry hears giggling from the <part>laundry pile</part>. Out pops her niece, socks on both hands as gloves, 'helping' by tossing shirts at the ceiling. She folds one towel into a crown, puts it on and bows. Every customer asks after the cheeky little <kanji>lass</kanji>.
嬢.on: She folds a tiny pouch for a <sound>jo</sound>ey that hopped in with the towels.
嬢.kun: '<sound>Mu</sound>!' says a cow at the window; the lass hangs a <sound>su</sound>it to dry on its horns and gives it some <sound>me</sound>lon.

旋.meaning: A bored giant at the swimming pool kicks the <part>diving board</part> with his <part>giant boot</part>. The board spins like a propeller, and a <part>sail</part> someone left on it catches the wind and keeps it whirling all summer. The kids ride it round and round. The pool's best ride is pure <kanji>rotation</kanji>.
旋.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try stands guard so nobody climbs on while it's spinning.
旋.kun: A <sound>me</sound>lon rolls off the end, and a <sound>goo</sound>se chases it round and round the pool.

較.meaning: At a crossroads, a shiny new <part>car</part> and a rusty old banger pull up side by side, and their drivers <part>mingle</part>, chatting window to window. Everyone on the pavement looks from one to the other: gleaming paint, dangling bumper. The two cars are a perfect <kanji>contrast</kanji>.
較.on: On the old car's roof sits a vulture, picking at a chicken <sound>car</sound>cass.
較.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo on a lamppost looks them both over, then shouts '<sound>Rah</sound>!' for the rusty one.

喚.meaning: Grandad opens a birthday present. Out springs a <part>jack-in-the-box</part> with a huge painted <part>mouth</part>, so suddenly that his glasses fly across the room. He leaps onto the sofa and lets out the loudest <kanji>yell</kanji> the street has ever heard.
喚.on: To say sorry, the toy holds out a pink <sound>car</sound>nation in its spring.
喚.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' he howls again, and hides behind a <sound>me</sound>lon in the fruit bowl.

摂.meaning: An old sailor can't go to sea any more. He drops a toy <part>anchor</part> in his bath, holds a radio to his <part>ear</part> for his grandson's reports from the frozen north and sucks chips of <part>ice</part> to feel the cold. He's on every voyage, but his adventures are all <kanji>vicarious</kanji>.
摂.on: His red <sound>set</sound>ter lies by the tub and shivers along with him.
摂.kun: He hangs the radio on a little <sound>to</sound>tem pole beside the tub to take in every word.

搭.meaning: A traveller's <part>picnic basket</part> is so heavy that she hooks it to the ship's <part>anchor</part> chain and lets the winch haul it up, with her clinging to the handle. The gulls cheer as she swings over the rail. It's the strangest way anyone has ever chosen to <kanji>board</kanji>.
搭.on: She lands on the deck with a bump and stubs her <sound>toe</sound>.

昆.meaning: Great-grandma eats breakfast in the <part>sun</part> on her porch with <part>two spoons</part>: one for her and one for whoever is youngest. Over the years the second spoon passes from her son to her grandson to his tiny twins. That spoon has fed all her <kanji>descendants</kanji>.
昆.on: A <sound>con</sound>dor watches from the roof, hoping someone drops a spoonful.

醜.meaning: A vain <part>ghost</part> tries to scare a party with a stick of <part>dynamite</part>. It fizzles and goes off with a puff, and he's left with a sooty sheet, singed eyebrows and hair sticking up. The guests don't scream; they hand him a mirror. Even he finds himself <kanji>ugly</kanji>.
醜.on: He tries to wipe off the soot with an old <sound>shoe</sound>.
醜.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat laughs so hard it bangs its <sound>knee</sound>, and the <sound>coo</sound>k brings it ice.

弊.meaning: The coach's best silk shirt is torn into a <part>rag</part> to scrub mud off the <part>goal</part> posts. Then the team uses the sleeves to tie up the net and the collar to polish their boots. The poor shirt has suffered nothing but <kanji>abuse</kanji>.
弊.on: What's left of it gets stuffed under a pile of <sound>hay</sound> behind the goal.

培.meaning: Every morning a gardener climbs onto a <part>soapbox</part> beside her vegetable patch and gives the seedlings a pep talk: 'Grow, beans, grow!' Then she digs compost into the <part>soil</part> and waters every row. Speeches and spadework: that's how she likes to <kanji>cultivate</kanji> a garden.
培.on: She rides her <sound>bi</sound>ke between the rows to check who's listening.
培.kun: The dust makes her sneeze, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and she buries <sound>chee</sound>se rind and old <sound>ca</sound>rp bones to feed the soil.
